status: formal first version for development review; not yet frozen for bulk annotation
definition: Coverage is the requirement-level profile of all causally available evidence before the current order relative to the current question.
unit: one entry per answer requirement declared by the current primary or secondary question

required_fields.requirement_key: unique per-question instance key; coverage must match the declared answer requirement by this key
required_fields.requirement_id: must match an answer requirement declared in the linked question
required_fields.supporting_evidence: zero or more exact quotations from evidence visible before the current order
required_fields.reason: brief explanation of why the cited evidence gives this status and direction

aggregate.rule: The aggregate is optional shorthand and never replaces requirement entries. Sufficiently answered normally requires every decision-critical requirement to be sufficiently addressed; document any exception.

decision_rules: The same requirement_id may occur more than once when the concrete information object differs; each occurrence must have a unique requirement_key and object-specific dimension.
Evaluate all evidence visible before the current order, not only the most recent study.
A requirement is unaddressed when no visible evidence actually examines that dimension.
A requirement is partially addressed when relevant evidence exists but is limited, incomplete, conflicting, indirect, or does not cover the full target.
A requirement is sufficiently addressed when the available evidence adequately covers the dimension for the current decision, whether its direction supports or refutes the question.
A valid negative can be sufficiently addressed with direction=refutes.
Nonvisualization, nondiagnostic examination, and not-assessed anatomy are not valid negatives and normally leave the corresponding requirement unaddressed or partially addressed.
Study adequacy, test-question capability, result status, and aggregate coverage are separate judgments and must not be inferred from one another without an explicit link.
Coverage is question-relative: one study may sufficiently address one requirement while leaving another requirement unaddressed.

boundary_examples.case: A technically diagnostic pelvic ultrasound evaluates the ovary but not the appendix.
boundary_examples.decision: study_adequacy=diagnostic; ovarian requirement may be sufficiently_addressed; appendix target_visualization_or_assessment remains unaddressed; appendix result_status=not_assessed.

boundary_examples.case: The appendix is adequately visualized and no inflammatory abnormality is present.
boundary_examples.decision: target visualization and presence/absence may be sufficiently_addressed with direction=refutes and result_status=negative.

boundary_examples.case: The appendix is not visualized because of bowel gas or body habitus.
boundary_examples.decision: study_adequacy is limited or nondiagnostic for that target; result_status is indeterminate or not_assessed; do not mark the disease excluded.

boundary_examples.case: One scan shows inflammation while later clinical and laboratory evidence weakens that interpretation.
boundary_examples.decision: Preserve the requirement-level evidence with direction=mixed; do not force a single support/refute label for the whole question.

supporting_evidence: Prior imaging: appendix was not visualized
requirements.reason: The target was sought but not adequately assessed.
No valid positive or negative assessment of the appendix is available.

machine_contract_example.aggregate_reason: The decision-critical presence/absence requirement remains open.
